history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: Bibrod Tirth is a Jain (Shwetambar) pilgrimage site at Bibrod/Bibdod village near Ratlam - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. The tirth's moolnayak is Shri Adinath Bhagwan (first Tirthankara), per the Gujarat/Madhya Pradesh Jain tirth directories (moolnayak: Shree Adinath Bhagwan), and the complex is also listed as Adinath Jain Swarn Tirth on MDR 12A at Bibrod. It is a recognised Shwetambar pilgrim halt with dharamshala facilities, not an ancient temple: no dated construction or patron dynasty is recorded in the sources consulted. CSV correction: the 'town' is not Ratlam city but Bibrod (also spelled Bibdod/Bimbdod) village, Ratlam sub-district, a few km from Ratlam Junction; documented accordingly.

name: Bibrod Tirth
town_description: Bibrod (also Bibdod/Bimbdod) is a village in Ratlam sub-district, Madhya Pradesh, a few kilometres from Ratlam city on the Ratlam-area district roads (MDR 12A), best known for its Jain tirth.
tradition: Jainism (Shwetambar) - NOT a Hindu temple; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (~140 km) is the nearest commercial airport.
travel.railway: Ratlam Junction is the nearest major railway station (~7-8 km), on the Delhi-Mumbai corridor.
travel.road: Reachable by road from Ratlam via the district road (MDR 12A); local buses and taxis available from Ratlam city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahavir Jayanti and Paryushan are the main pilgrim occasions.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typical Jain temple darshan hours (morning and evening); published hours not found in consulted sources (verify). Dharamshala accommodation is available for pilgrims.
